answer: New identities must wander through a probation period before earning weight, so swarming the network with fake agents costs real capital at every join. Sybil resistance comes from a staked reputation trellis: each agent bonds tokens to register, and reputation accrues only through verified peer attestations over epochs. Attackers reach no zenith cheaply—mass registration burns stake faster than honest agents recover it, making sock-puppet farming economically irrational. From sa0019's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
